title: Chart: A record two-thirds of car sales in China are now electric vehicles - Carbon Brief
gist: CPCA data show NEVs reached a record 67% of China's new car sales in September 2026. The share rose because combustion-car sales collapsed (-43% y/y) during the Hormuz-driven oil price spike, even though NEV sales fell 17%. NEV exports jumped 164% y/y to 558,000 units, and an AlixPartners partner expects the NEV share to stay below 80%.

themes.theme: Record NEV share on a shrinking market

insights.claim: New-energy vehicles were a record 67% of new car sales in China in September 2026, according to the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA). The NEV share was 58% in 2026 to date, up from 6% in 2020.
insights.speaker: Lekai Liu
insights.so_what: China's ICE car market is in terminal decline, which is structurally bearish for gasoline demand and for ICE-focused automakers and suppliers.
insights.quote: For the first time, new-energy vehicles (NEVs) made up 67% of new car sales in China in September
insights.locator: For the first time, new-energy vehicles

insights.claim: China's passenger-car retail sales fell 28% year-on-year in September 2026. Combustion-engine sales fell 43% in September and 31% in 2026 to date.
insights.speaker: Lekai Liu
insights.so_what: A sharp contraction in the domestic auto market is a demand shock for Chinese automakers and their supply chains.
insights.quote: The contraction was led by combustion-engine vehicles, which saw sales fall 43% year-on-year in September and 31% in 2026 to date.
insights.locator: The contraction was led by combustion-engine

insights.claim: Battery EVs outperformed plug-in hybrids in China in 2026. In September PHEV sales fell 36% y/y and BEV sales fell 8.5%; in 2026 to date PHEVs fell 26% and BEVs 4%. Total NEV sales fell 17% in September and 13% year to date.
insights.speaker: Lekai Liu
insights.so_what: The mix is shifting toward pure BEVs, which favours BEV-focused makers and battery demand over hybrid platforms.
insights.quote: However, sales of PHEVs also fell by 36% year-on-year in September and by 26% in 2026 to date.
insights.locator: However, sales of PHEVs also fell

insights.claim: The NEV share dropped to 39% in January 2026 after China's more-than-decade-long full purchase tax exemption ended in December 2025, then recovered to record levels.
insights.speaker: Lekai Liu
insights.so_what: The rebound shows NEV adoption is now resilient without subsidies.
insights.quote: This year, NEVs’ share of sales has also bounced back from a low of 39% in January
insights.locator: This year, NEVs’ share of sales

insights.claim: Sales of combustion-engine cars in China peaked in 2017 and have declined every year since.
insights.speaker: Lekai Liu
insights.so_what: The 2026 collapse accelerates a decade-long structural trend rather than reflecting a one-off shock.
insights.quote: Indeed, sales of combustion-engine cars in China peaked in 2017 and they have been declining ever since

insights.claim: CPCA secretary-general Cui Dongshu attributed the weak combustion-car sales in September 2026 to higher petrol prices following the start of the Hormuz crisis.
insights.speaker: Cui Dongshu
insights.so_what: Oil price shocks translate directly into EV substitution in China, which makes oil demand more elastic than historical models assume.
insights.quote: Cui Dongshu, secretary-general of the CPCA, cited higher petrol prices as an explanation for September’s weak combustion-car sales
insights.locator: Cui Dongshu, secretary-general of the CPCA

insights.claim: China's oil imports fell 15% in January-September 2026 compared with 2025, equivalent to 470m barrels, as the conflict tightened supply and raised prices.
insights.speaker: Lekai Liu
insights.so_what: Weaker crude demand from the world's largest importer is a key variable for oil prices and tanker volumes.
insights.quote: Imports of oil into China in January-September have fallen 15% compared to 2025, equivalent to 470m barrels

insights.claim: According to Ember senior energy analyst Euan Graham, China's passenger-car NEV fleet has displaced 143m barrels of oil since the start of the Strait of Hormuz crisis.
insights.speaker: Euan Graham
insights.so_what: The EV fleet is a growing, measurable source of structural oil demand destruction in China.
insights.quote: China’s passenger-car NEV fleet has displaced 143m barrels of oil so far during the strait of Hormuz crisis
insights.locator: China’s passenger-car NEV fleet has displaced

insights.claim: An unnamed analyst estimated for the Brookings Institute that EVs accounted for 12% of the decrease in China's oil use after Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Lekai Liu
insights.so_what: EVs explain only part of China's oil demand drop; price-driven demand destruction and import cuts explain the rest.
insights.quote: EVs “accounted for 12% of the decrease in China’s oil use post-Hormuz”

insights.claim: Columbia University's Erica Downs says the Hormuz crisis, which she calls the world's largest oil supply disruption, reinforces China's electrification of road transport and vindicates its early EV bet, which was partly motivated by oil-supply security.
insights.speaker: Erica Downs
insights.so_what: Energy-security motives will keep Chinese policy support for EVs firm, and other oil importers may follow.
insights.quote: the strait of Hormuz crisis and higher oil prices are “reinforcing China’s electrification of road transport”
insights.locator: Erica Downs, a senior research scholar

themes.theme: Headwinds to NEV demand and a share ceiling

insights.claim: Consulting firm Wood Mackenzie attributes weak NEV demand to purchases pulled forward into 2025 before subsidies ended, and to tighter financing conditions.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Part of the 2026 weakness is a payback for the 2025 pull-forward and may ease next year.
insights.quote: weakened demand due to “demand pull-forward” in 2025 caused by the end of subsidies, as well as “tighter financing conditions”
insights.locator: Other factors, says consulting firm Wood

insights.claim: AlixPartners partner Zhang Yichao says NEVs benefit from government trade-in policies and a strong pipeline of new models. He does not see much more room for share growth and thinks the NEV share in China is unlikely to exceed 80%, because premium segments and some use cases will still need combustion engines.
insights.speaker: Zhang Yichao
insights.so_what: With the share already at 67%, future NEV volume growth in China depends on overall market growth rather than share gains.
insights.quote: their share in China is unlikely to exceed 80%
insights.locator: He adds that, in his view

insights.claim: Cui Dongshu also attributed the September 2026 decline to a high baseline from September 2025, changes to trade-in policies and holiday disruptions.
insights.speaker: Cui Dongshu
insights.so_what: Base effects flatter the year-on-year decline, so underlying demand may be less weak than the headline suggests.
insights.locator: Cui told the state-run China National Radio

themes.theme: NEV export surge and trade friction

insights.claim: China's NEV exports rose 164% year-on-year in September 2026, while domestic NEV retail sales fell 17%. In September 1,084,000 NEVs were sold domestically and 558,000 were exported.
insights.speaker: Lekai Liu
insights.so_what: Exports are now a third of NEV volume, which raises the stakes of foreign tariff decisions for Chinese automakers.
insights.quote: In September, 1,084,000 NEVs were sold domestically in China, while 558,000 NEVs were exported.

insights.claim: Faced with weak domestic demand and cut-throat competition, some Chinese carmakers have made exports a core priority, according to the CPCA.
insights.speaker: China Passenger Car Association
insights.so_what: Chinese overcapacity is being exported, which adds competitive pressure on legacy automakers in emerging markets and Europe.
insights.quote: The CPCA says exports have become “a core priority” for some carmakers.
insights.locator: The CPCA says exports have become

insights.claim: The EU has put tariffs on Chinese EV imports and recently agreed plans to cut hybrid imports, and Mexico and Turkey also impose tariffs. Meanwhile China is cutting VAT export rebates, and analysts disagree on whether this will raise exported car prices.
insights.speaker: Lekai Liu
insights.so_what: Tariff escalation plus rebate cuts threaten the export outlet that offsets weak domestic sales.
insights.quote: the Chinese government is putting policies in place that might be expected to disincentivise exports, such as cutting VAT export rebates
